story_type: swift-water rescue training in snowmelt rapids
hook: Snowmelt rapids, one rope, and a man held in the white water.
narration: The current flipped him upside down, and the rope held him right there.
This was training. Marine mountain warfare instructors, in a fast California river.
Their job is to pull other troops out of water exactly like this.
So first, they swam the rapids themselves, again and again.
In fast water you float on your back, feet first, so your legs meet the rocks before your head does.
Then a man went into the worst of the white water, on the end of a line.
The river piled over his helmet, again and again, while the rope held him in place.
[short pause] Then a swimmer went out through the current to reach him.
Together, the team walked him back across to the bank.
outcome: Every instructor left that river trained to pull a fellow Marine out of fast water.
title: Held on a rope in snowmelt rapids
description:
Marine mountain warfare instructors trained in swift-water rescue in a fast river at the Marine Corps Mountain Warfare Training Center in Bridgeport, California, on April 19, 2019, learning to rescue other service members from fast moving water.
